title: Projective amplitude of a pseudo-coherent complex is equivalent to perfection with bounded tor amplitude and to Ext vanishing against finitely presented modules
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, a pseudo-coherent object K of D(R), and integers a and b, and establishes the equivalence of five conditions: that K have projective-amplitude in [a, b]; that K be perfect of tor-amplitude in [a, b]; that Ext^i_R(K, N) vanish for all finitely presented N and all i outside [-b, -a]; that H^n(K) vanish for n > b with Ext^i_R(K, N) vanishing for all finitely presented N and all i > -a; and that H^n(K) vanish outside [a-1, b] with Ext^{-a+1}_R(K, N) vanishing for all finitely presented N (source lines 20135-20150). The proof is organized in two halves. First, (2) implies (1) by the final statement of the perfect-complex lemma; conversely, if (1) holds then K is represented by a complex of projectives P^i vanishing outside [a, b], and since projective modules are flat being summands of free modules, K has tor-amplitude in [a, b], so (2) holds (proof lines 20153-20158). The substantive second half reduces the Ext conditions against finitely presented modules to conditions against all modules: the proof observes that in (3), (4) and (5) the assumed vanishing of Ext^i_R(K, M) for M of finite presentation is equivalent to the vanishing for all R-modules M, by the colimit statement for pseudo-coherent objects together with the description of an arbitrary module as a filtered colimit of finitely presented ones (proof lines 20161-20165). The equivalence of (1), (3), (4) and (5) then follows from the projective-amplitude criterion (proof lines 20166-20167). The non-routine content is the reduction of the Ext vanishing hypotheses from finitely presented to arbitrary modules, which is what brings the three numerical conditions into the range of the existing criterion.
